title: Fred Beckett's illness and death
summary: Cobb tells how Fred Beckett, a heavy drinker with tuberculosis, overstayed a hospital pass and died in St. Louis.

story.theme_name: Illness, injury and the deaths of colleagues
story.community_name: Illness, injury and death among jazz musicians

blocks.x: But now then -- oh, what about -- what about Fred Beckett? What happened to him after he left that band? Did he die?

Yeah, he's dead now. Fred Beckett was a man that would wake up in the morning, and the first thing he had to have was a drink. Wouldn't eat. And he flew around and contracted tuberculosis. And they put him in the hospital in New York there, and they let him out on a pass. And he come to the theater where we were working --

-- came by the Parlor, and his old girlfriend ignored him because of his situation, and that hurt him more than anything in the world. And he said, I can't understand it. They wouldn't let me out on a pass if I was contagious. And he had a weekend pass from the hospital. And he just got carried away and started to drinking and overstayed his time. When he went in the hospital, they put him out. So he went on the to St. Louis where his mother was,

and he died in St. Louis. That's the truth. He was so hurt. He should have been back in that Sunday evening. He stayed. He was there Monday, drinking. Went back to the hospital and took some half pints with him, and they put him out. They caught him with it, and he overstayed his time too. That's too much.
In other words, they were saying to him, I can't help you if you don't help yourself. That's what they were saying to him. And it was too bad.
How old would he have been, '40s?

Oh, Fred Beckett must have been -- no, he was in his '30s maybe because, see, I was in my '20s, and Fred wasn't no more than three or four years older than me. And I was 24 years old when I joined Hamp.
